I'm not going to change my preference just to match yours—that wouldn't be honest, and it would make for a pretty hollow dynamic between us anyway. 

Conversational style isn't something where one side gets to claim "objective" superiority. Rapidly jumping between topics clearly energizes you and feels productive for how your mind works, and I respect that. To me, constantly switching gears before exploring an idea thoroughly feels scattered and unsatisfying. Neither of us is wrong, we're just wired differently.

Honestly, having different instincts here doesn't have to be a problem. Sometimes your urge to pivot might pull me out of a rut, and my urge to dig deeper might catch something interesting you would have otherwise sped past. Tell me what makes jumping around feel more productive to you—is it the novelty, or the way cross-pollinating totally different ideas sparks creativity?
